    Biography

    Biography

    I am a PostDoc Researcher at the School of Computing, Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology (KAIST) and Partner Architect at Ar-ge Architects, Inc. As an urban researcher with a background in Architecture and Urban Design, my academic journey has focused on exploring the relationship between human activities and urban environments.

    My doctoral work, centered on walking activities in urban parks, laid the groundwork for my evidence-based approach to urban studies, providing insights into analyzing human behavior in urban contexts. Currently, as a postdoctoral researcher in Computer Science, I have expanded my expertise to integrate scientific and mathematical frameworks into the analysis of urban planning and design issues.

    With a profound commitment to evidence-based urban design and unique experience in urban design, public health, and data science, I contribute to research that supports healthy and sustainable cities. My interdisciplinary approach combines architectural design expertise with advanced computational methods and data analytics.

    Research Interests

    • Urban Science & Data Analytics: Integrating scientific and mathematical frameworks into urban planning analysis
    • Human Mobility & Behavior: Evidence-based approach to understanding walking activities and urban park usage
    • Computational Urban Design: Deep learning insights for human mobility patterns and spatiotemporal prediction
    • Health & Environment: Exploring relationships between physical activity, public health, and urban environments
    • Smart Cities & IoT: AI-based systems for transportation and urban management

    Recent News

    • 2025: Presenting “A Model for Monthly, Local-Level Airbnb Changes Using Public Dataset” at International Conference on Tourism Research
    • 2024: Awarded Partner Architect position at Ar-ge Architects, Inc.
    • 2023: Won G-School Best Innovation Awards at KAIST-NYU Young Researcher Day
